definition: Semantic queries allow for queries and analytics of associative and contextual nature.
details: Semantic queries enable the retrieval of both explicitly and implicitly derived information based on syntactic, semantic and structural information contained in data. They are designed to deliver precise results (possibly the distinctive selection of one single piece of information) or to answer more fuzzy and wide open questions through pattern matching and digital reasoning. Semantic queries work on named graphs, linked data or triples. This enables the query to process the actual relationships between information and infer the answers from the network of data. This is in contrast to semantic search, which uses semantics (meaning of language constructs) in unstructured text to produce a better search result. (See natural language processing.) From a technical point of view, semantic queries are precise relational-type operations much like a database query. They work on structured data and therefore have the possibility to utilize comprehensive features like operators (e.g. >, < and =), namespaces, pattern matching, subclassing, transitive relations, semantic rules and contextual full text search. explainer.lead: Semantic queries retrieve and analyze information by meaning and relationship rather than by exact record matching. They matter because they surface both explicit and implicitly derived facts from connected data.

tiers.eli5: Instead of looking up a word in an index, you ask how things are connected and get answers that follow those links.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run semantic queries over named graphs, linked data or triples so the query can follow actual relationships; a pitfall is that inference over large graphs can be slow or produce surprising implied results.
tiers.paperLevel: Queries allowing analytics of associative and contextual nature, retrieving explicitly and implicitly derived information from syntactic, semantic and structural data. They operate on named graphs, linked data or triples and may return precise single results or fuzzy answers via pattern matching and digital reasoning; performance and correctness depend on the underlying graph and its inference rules.

explainer.example: A query over a triple store finds every supplier of a part and also infers indirect suppliers through ownership links, returning both direct and derived results.
